hypothesis: The Riemann-Roch family never moved the oracle's EXPONENT. Both it and brute-force pair enumeration cost Theta(|F|^2) in the factor-base size, and the RR solver differs only by a constant factor greater than one. Stated sharply: RR_candidates(d) / (|F|^2 / 2) is bounded and roughly constant in d, rather than falling. If so, the whole thread -- solver_02 through solver_10 -- is a sequence of constant-factor improvements to a search whose order was never in question, and the background note's falsification target, which demands a speedup FACTOR of 2^(70.19 + log2 m) against C(|F|, m-1), is untouched by any of it.
why_this_is_the_method_ceiling: docs/inventor-protocol.md section 8 asks for a method ceiling before expensive experiments: the best possible outcome of the method as specified. For an m=3 decomposition oracle the candidate space is the set of summand pairs, and finding P1+P2+P3 = R with all Pi in F is exactly 3SUM over a group. Pair enumeration realises the generic Theta(|F|^2) bound. An oracle that only reorganises which pairs it visits cannot beat it in order; it can only change the constant and the per-candidate cost. Measuring that constant across several d says whether the RR encoding is exploiting the subspace structure of F or merely re-indexing a generic search.
curve: K_0 : y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131), ONB model, group order checked against the Koblitz recurrence as 4r. Identical to solver_10 and solver_12.
targets: Two planted targets per dimension, minted under seed 20260917 and recorded with their triples. Planted rather than uniform because the quantity under measurement is the SIZE of the exhausted candidate space, which a planted target exercises fully in enumerate mode; the uniform case was already measured in solver_10 and solver_12 and costs the same to exhaust.
method: For each d, run the frozen solver_08 quadratic-image solver in enumerate mode with a budget large enough to complete, and the solver_12 pair oracle on the same targets. Record, per instance: |F| (signed factor-base points), pairs enumerated, RR candidate functions, and counted field API operations for each. Then report RR_candidates / (|F|^2/2), pair_ops / RR_ops, and the growth exponent of each series against |F| by least squares on the logarithms.
primary_metric: The dimensionless ratio RR_candidates / (|F|^2 / 2) as a function of d, and the fitted exponent of each oracle's cost in |F|.
falsification: The hypothesis is falsified if the ratio RR_candidates / (|F|^2/2) FALLS with d, or if the fitted RR exponent in |F| is materially below 2. Either would mean the encoding is exploiting structure rather than re-indexing, and the thread would deserve the larger dimensions it has never been run at. It is confirmed if the ratio is roughly flat and above one.
limits: Budgets are chosen per dimension to let both oracles COMPLETE, so this measures candidate-space size, not what fits in a fixed budget; it is deliberately not the matched-budget question solver_10 answered. Five dimensions spanning |F| by about an order of magnitude is a short lever arm for an exponent fit, and the admissible-abscissa count fluctuates with d, so |F| rather than 2^d is the regressor. A flat ratio is evidence about THIS encoding and this arity, not a lower bound on all decomposition oracles: a genuinely sub-quadratic oracle exploiting the subspace structure is not excluded by anything measured here, and 3SUM hardness is a conjecture about generic sets that an algebraically structured F need not obey. No attack cost, yield, S or rho ratio is computed.
